newsitem.title: USA: Hung jury in John Denver's drunken driving case.
newsitem.headline: Hung jury in John Denver's drunken driving case.

text.p: The trial of singer John Denver on drunk driving charges stemming from a car accident in 1994 ended in a hung jury, the singer's lawyer said on Sunday.
"The jury came in at 10:20 Saturday night (0420 GMT Sunday). They were deadlocked 3-3 on impaired (charges)," Walter Gerash told Reuters by telephone from Aspen, where the three-day trial was held.
Gerash said the judge set an Aug. 19 date to reschedule the case or dispose of the matter.

Denver, who was hugely popular in the 1970s with such hit songs as "Rocky Mountain High," was charged with driving under the influence in August 1994 after he slammed his yellow Porsche into a tree in an exclusive area near Aspen. He was treated at a local hospital for a seven-inch cut on his head.
The defence argued that Denver has a thyroid condition that causes him to metabolise food and drink at half the normal rate.
Denver's blood alcohol level tested two hours after the accident at 0.128, above Colorado's legal definition of being under the influence of alcohol.
Gerash said the six-person jury included a physician and an orthodonist.
